A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CuMA research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the retained Appendices A–F and new Appendices G–I.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, demographic generalization results, routing visualizations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds baseline generalization comparisons, a human evaluation audit, inference profiling, and routing-overlap measurements.

M1.justification: The demographic encoder, joint semantic-demographic router, Top-k LoRA experts, and SFT/DPO/GRPO objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and implementation details describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds GSM8K mathematical queries as a consensus-task contrast to WVB for routing-overlap analysis. Existing cultural benchmarks and held-out demographic coverage remain intact; no GSM8K answer-accuracy evaluation is reported.

E2.justification: New Table 3 adds LoRA, DoRA, P-Tuning v2, MixLoRA, and HydraLoRA to the existing held-out demographic comparison, which previously reported only CuMA. The main benchmark comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation procedures through a blinded, reference-based audit of 100 samples by five researchers, batch-size-1 inference profiling, and cross-demographic routing-overlap measurement. These are protocols for added analyses; the original training settings, data splits, and benchmark evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices G–I add analyses addressing automated-judge reliability, practical inference costs, and whether routing shares experts for consensus tasks while separating cultural preferences. Table 3 strengthens the existing generalization analysis with baseline comparisons. Earlier component ablations and Top-k-versus-soft-routing experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly reports Cohen’s kappa for expert–GPT-4o agreement. Appendix H states that efficiency measurements average three independent runs. Original benchmark results retain their point-estimate reporting; these additions do not establish additional runs of the earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 and cluster-level Table 2 scores are unchanged, but substantial new results cover baseline transfer, human auditing, efficiency, and routing overlap. Examples include sample-weighted zero-shot accuracy of 48.10% for CuMA versus 36.24% for HydraLoRA, and routing overlap of 76.4% on GSM8K versus 18.2% on WVB. Section 5.1 also corrects FFT accuracy from 44.20% to the retained table value of 45.25%.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1, Theorem 2.1, and the assumptions and conclusions of Appendix B are retained. B.2 compresses equivalent derivation steps and renumbers equations without changing the reasoning. The standard kappa formula and operational routing-overlap measure do not add theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about cultural sparsity, mean collapse, demographic-aware capacity separation, and cultural-alignment performance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking English-speaking transfer performance to pre-training representation and cultural compactness, and interprets routing overlap as adaptive sharing versus separation. The limitations replace the claim of latency comparable to dense models with acknowledged inference overhead supported by Appendix H.

D1.justification: V2 documents profiling on one RTX PRO 6000 96GB GPU with batch size 1 and identifies the profiled CuMA rank-8 variant. It also explicitly distinguishes cluster macro-averaging from the new sample-weighted comparison. Existing architecture details, hyperparameters, prompts, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cobbe et al. (2021) for GSM8K and removes Adilazuarda et al. (2025), 'From surveys to narratives,' replacing its citations with the existing 2024 survey. Most other reference edits concern the same works’ bibliographic metadata; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local revisions clarify consensus versus non-consensus tasks, ambient dimensionality, and entropy versus diversity, while shortening the B.2 exposition. Author order, affiliations, acknowledgments, and bibliography are updated. Appendices G–I are added without reorganizing the established narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3, 6, and 7 for generalization comparisons, human auditing, and efficiency. Table 2’s average label and caption are clarified, and existing tables are renumbered or repositioned. The four figures and overall two-column presentation are retained.

improvement.justification: Matched zero-shot comparisons, human auditing, inference measurements, and routing analysis strengthen validation and transparency beyond v1. The gains are limited by the small reference-based audit and sparse routing-analysis details. Aggregation also remains insufficiently explained: Table 3’s zero-shot EMD of 0.2100 is below every Table 2 cluster value despite the weighted-average explanation.
